title: IMO MSC.428(98) Document of Compliance (DoC) cyber-SMS verification register + flag-State annual-verification clock with cyber-major-non-conformity risk score
exclusions: Excludes vessels under interim DoC (less than 90 days from delivery). Excludes vessels operating under flag-of-convenience non-IMO-member registries (rare but possible). Excludes lay-up vessels with cold-stack status.
evidence: Saved search `UC-22.59.1` archived daily to `audit_evidence` with `imo_clause="IMO-MSC-428-98-p2"`. Every row pins (imo_number, ship_name, flag_state, recognised_organisation, doc_issue_date, last_annual_verification, next_due_date, cyber_sms_attestation_status, cyber_sms_evidence_artefact, days_to_next_verification, risk_score).

compliance.assurance_rationale: IMO MSC.428(98) §2 requires that cyber risks be appropriately addressed in the safety management system no later than the first annual verification of the company's Document of Compliance after 1 January 2021. This UC implements the fleet-wide DoC verification register, attests cyber-SMS readiness ahead of each verification, and surfaces the gap risk in time for the DPA to act.
compliance.controlObjective: Demonstrates that the company maintains a complete DoC verification register, that every fleet vessel has a current cyber-risk-managed SMS attestation, and that the next annual verification is on track without cyber-major-non-conformity risk.
compliance.evidenceArtifact: Saved search archived to `audit_evidence`, the `IMO DoC Cyber-SMS Verification Health` dashboard, the flag-State verification certificates, and the RO (recognised-organisation) verification reports.

compliance.assurance_rationale: ISM Code §1.4 sets functional requirements for an SMS; MSC.428(98) extends these to include cyber. This UC closes the cyber-SMS attestation loop that the flag State and RO verify.
compliance.controlObjective: Evidences that the cyber-SMS attestation is current at each annual DoC verification.

controlTest.positiveScenario: UC-22.59.1 positive (IMO, MSC.428(98), Document, Compliance, (DoC)): ingest synthetic events into `index=target_index` sourcetype='target_sourcetype' where `count` grouped by `entity` satisfies `days_since_attestation` > 365, `days_since_attestation` > 335, `days_to_next_verification` <= 30, or `days_to_next_verification` <= 90 for 'IMO MSC.428(98) Document of Compliance (DoC) cyber-SMS verification register + flag-State annual-verification clock with cyber-major-non-conformity risk score'.  Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row.
controlTest.negativeScenario: UC-22.59.1 negative (risk score): ingest benign `target_index` / `target_sourcetype` events where `entity` stays below `days_since_attestation` > 365, `days_since_attestation` > 335, `days_to_next_verification` <= 30, or `days_to_next_verification` <= 90, or exclude the test entity via `compliance_exception_register.csv`. Variant 0 confirms zero alert rows for 'IMO MSC.428(98) Document of Compliance (DoC) cyber-SMS verification register + flag-State annual-verification clock with cyber-major-non-conformity risk score'.

dataSources: KV Store `imo_doc_verification_lookup` (imo_number, ship_name, flag_state, recognised_organisation, doc_issue_date, last_annual_verification, next_due_date, cyber_sms_attestation_status, cyber_sms_evidence_artefact, dpa_signed_at, dpa_signature_hash). ServiceNow CMDB fleet inventory (`snow:cmdb_ci`). Flag-State / RO portals (HEC `hec:imo:flag:submission`).
app: Splunk Enterprise Security (Splunkbase 263), Splunk Add-on for ServiceNow (Splunkbase 1928), Splunk Common Information Model Add-on (Splunkbase 1621).
spl:
| inputlookup imo_doc_verification_lookup
| eval now_ts = now()
| eval days_to_next_verification = round((next_due_date - now_ts) / 86400, 1)
| eval days_since_attestation = case(isnotnull(dpa_signed_at), round((now_ts - dpa_signed_at) / 86400, 1), 1=1, null)
| eval cyber_sms_attestation_status = case(
    isnull(dpa_signed_at), "missing",
    days_since_attestation > 365, "expired",
    days_since_attestation > 335, "renewal-due",
    1=1, "current")
| eval risk_score = case(
    cyber_sms_attestation_status = "missing" AND days_to_next_verification <= 30, 100,
    cyber_sms_attestation_status = "missing" AND days_to_next_verification <= 90, 90,
    cyber_sms_attestation_status = "expired" AND days_to_next_verification <= 30, 95,
    cyber_sms_attestation_status = "expired", 80,
    cyber_sms_attestation_status = "renewal-due" AND days_to_next_verification <= 30, 70,
    cyber_sms_attestation_status = "renewal-due", 40,
    cyber_sms_attestation_status = "current" AND days_to_next_verification < 0, 60,
    1=1, 0)
| where risk_score > 0
| sort 0 -risk_score, +days_to_next_verification
| table imo_number ship_name flag_state recognised_organisation doc_issue_date last_annual_verification next_due_date days_to_next_verification cyber_sms_attestation_status days_since_attestation risk_score
description: Monitors 'IMO MSC.428(98) Document of Compliance (DoC) cyber-SMS verification register + flag-State annual-verification clock with cyber-major-non-conformity risk score' (UC-22.59.1) using `index=target_index` sourcetype `configured sourcetype` by aggregating `count` grouped by `entity` over `the scheduled window` and alerting when `days_since_attestation` > 365, `days_since_attestation` > 335, `days_to_next_verification` <= 30, or `days_to_next_verification` <= 90. Keywords: IMO, MSC.428(98), Document, Compliance, (DoC). Focuses on risk score behaviour so compliance teams can triage UC-22.59.1 without ad-hoc log review.
value: UC-22.59.1 accelerates insight into risk score ('IMO MSC.428(98) Document of Compliance (DoC) cyber-SMS verification register + flag-State annual-verification clock with cyber-major-non-conformity risk score') by tracking `activity` on UC-22.59.1 search results, reducing audit findings, regulatory gaps, and attestation delays before spreadsheet checks hide regressions.
implementation: (1) Populate `imo_doc_verification_lookup` from the company's fleet-management system (Veson Nautical IMOS, Dataloy, Star IPS) or from the RO portal (DNV ShipManager Hull, ABS Eagle, LR Class Direct). (2) The DPA signs a digital cyber-SMS attestation at the start of each verification cycle; the signature hash and timestamp are written to the KV Store. (3) Schedule UC-22.59.1 daily at 06:00 ship-local; route `risk_score >= 80` to the DPA + CISO at severity P1, `risk_score >= 60` at severity P2. (4) Build the `IMO DoC Cyber-SMS Verification Health` dashboard with per-flag-State, per-RO, and per-fleet-segment views.
visualization: (Panel 1) Fleet-wide cyber-SMS attestation status (missing / expired / renewal-due / current) — stacked bar by flag State. (Panel 2) Time-to-next-verification heatmap (vessel × days). (Panel 3) Open major-non-conformity-risk vessels sorted by risk_score. (Panel 4) 12-month attestation-renewal performance trend.

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Authorised IMO MSC 428 98 control testing** — Internal audit exercises 'IMO MSC.428(98) Document of Compliance (DoC) cyber-SMS verification register + flag-State annual-verification clock with cyber-major-non-conformity risk score' (UC-22.59.1) on `entity` during scheduled clause IMO-MSC-428-98-p2 sampling. Match compliance programme calendar.

2. **External assessor sampling** — QSA activity spikes `index=audit_evidence` `configured sourcetype` without crossing `days_since_attestation` > 365. Cross-check engagement letter in `imo_msc_428_98_exception_register.csv`.

3. **Planned maintenance affecting control telemetry** — CAB change pauses ingestion to `audit_evidence` for `entity`. Compare `_time` with active change record.

4. **Third-party processor under contract** — BAA/DPA-covered vendor generates expected rows grouped by `entity` during normal service delivery.

**Suppression mechanism:** `imo_msc_428_98_exception_register.csv` keyed on `entity`, `exception_reason`, `valid_until`, joined before alert threshold.

detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites

- Splunk Enterprise >= 9.2 or Splunk Cloud.
- KV Store `imo_doc_verification_lookup` (created via `collections.conf` and seeded from the fleet-management system).
- ServiceNow CMDB with vessel-level inventory (`cmdb_ci_vessel` or equivalent).
- Optional: HEC token for flag-State / RO portal callback integration (`hec:imo:flag:submission`).

## Step 1 — DoC Verification KV Store

```ini
[imo_doc_verification_lookup]
enforceTypes = true
field.imo_number = string
field.ship_name = string
field.flag_state = string
field.recognised_organisation = string
field.doc_issue_date = time
field.last_annual_verification = time
field.next_due_date = time
field.cyber_sms_attestation_status = string
field.cyber_sms_evidence_artefact = string
field.dpa_signed_at = time
field.dpa_signature_hash = string
field.vessel_status = string
```

Seed from the fleet-management system on a daily schedule (modular input or `outputlookup`).

## Step 2 — DPA Cyber-SMS Attestation

Provide the DPA with a quarterly attestation workflow that, on signature, writes a row into the KV Store with the timestamp, the signature hash, and a reference to the cyber-SMS evidence package (typically the company's most recent annual cyber-risk review).

## Step 3 — Schedule

```ini
[UC-22.59.1: IMO DoC Cyber-SMS Verification]
cron_schedule = 0 6 * * *
dispatch.earliest_time = -1d@d
dispatch.latest_time = now
actions = summary_index, notable
action.summary_index._name = audit_evidence
action.summary_index.marker = uc=22.59.1,reg=IMO-MSC-428-98,clause=IMO-MSC-428-98-p2
alert.severity = 5
```

## Step 4 — Runbooks

**`risk_score >= 80`** (owner: DPA, severity P1): Within 24 hours, schedule a DPA + CISO call with the vessel's Master / CSO to assess remediation; within 7 days, deliver a written remediation plan with an attestation date that pre-empts the DoC verification.

**`risk_score 40-79`** (owner: DPA, severity P2): Within 5 business days, drive an attestation refresh.

## Step 5 — Troubleshooting

- **Flag-State change**: when a vessel re-flags, the cyber-SMS attestation typically must be re-signed against the new flag administration's interpretation; allow a 30-day grace.
- **RO change**: similar to flag-State change.
- **Newbuild integration**: newbuild vessels delivered after 1 July 2024 carry IACS UR E26 class notation; integrate UC-22.59.14 cross-reference.

**Maritime-specific failure modes**:
- **Sub-IMO-tonnage vessel**: vessels below GT < 500 are typically outside SOLAS/ISM scope; ensure the vessel filter excludes these.
- **Inland-waterway operation**: rivers and lakes may operate under regional regimes (CCNR for Rhine, Mississippi River Basin for US inland barges) rather than IMO; segregate fleets.
- **Domestic-only operation**: some flag administrations apply IMO-equivalent regimes to domestic-only ships; consult flag-State guidance.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (Splunk Enterprise Security (Splunkbase 263), Splunk Add-on for ServiceNow (Splunkbase 1928), Splunk Common Information Model Add-on (Splunkbase 1621).). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=see SPL into index=main. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`cyber_sms_attestation_status, days_since_attestation, days_to_next_verification, risk_score`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: Every ship has an annual safety check by its flag country. Since 2021, that check also covers cyber risk. We watch which ships are coming up for their check and make sure each one has its cyber paperwork ready, so the ship isn't held in port or pulled out of service.
